10.1021/acs.iecr.6c04260.abstract: Abstract As a low-toxic and environmentally benign organic chemical feedstock, dimethyl carbonate exhibits widespread applications in numerous fields. Accordingly, the development of highly efficient and stable catalysts constitutes a key research focus for dimethyl carbonate synthesis. Recently, single-atom-based catalysts have emerged as a frontier in heterogeneous catalysis witnessing rapid development. Despite the considerable potential of single-atom-based catalysts for dimethyl carbonate synthesis, comprehensive and systematic overviews of the relevant research progress remain insufficient. Therefore, this review comprehensively summarizes the advances in single-atom-based catalysts for the synthesis of dimethyl carbonate via routes including transesterification, methanol oxidative carbonylation, methyl nitrite carbonylation, and electrosynthesis, while elaborating on their preparation strategies, catalytic performance, and reaction mechanisms. Meanwhile, this review proposes future directions for the development of single-atom-based catalysts used in dimethyl carbonate synthesis. This work is expected to provide guidance for designing high-performance single-atom-based catalysts toward efficient dimethyl carbonate synthesis.

10.1021/acs.inorgchem.6c03968.abstract: Abstract The addition of [Au(acac)(PMe3)] (acac = acetylacetonate) to orotic acid affords the mononuclear complex [Au(N-orotate)(PMe3)] (1) and the dinuclear species [{Au(PMe3)}2(μ-O,N-orotate)] (2), with the crystal structures of two polymorphs of complex 2 fully elucidated by X-ray diffraction studies. Remarkably, complex 1 undergoes ultrasound-induced supramolecular self-assembly in water to form a robust Au(I) hydrometallogel (1-hyd), whereas 2 lacks the capacity to gelate due to coordination-induced suppression of intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The hydrometallogel acts as both a soft template and an in situ gold precursor, enabling the formation of densely packed, belt-like assemblies of plasmonic Au nanoparticles (1-hyd-Au NPs) upon mild and short thermal treatment. These anisotropic nanoarrays display strong interparticle coupling, yielding a broad, red-shifted localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) absorption centered at ca. 650 nm with substantial NIR absorption. Under 808 nm excitation, the system exhibits efficient photothermal conversion accompanied by the generation of localized plasmonic hot spots. Exploiting this dual activation mode, 1-hyd-Au NPs photocatalyse the methanolysis of ammonia-borane, delivering significantly enhanced H2 release relative to purely thermal conditions. The results demonstrate that hydrometallogel-templated Au assemblies provide an effective and modular platform for NIR-driven plasmonic catalysis, integrating supramolecular templating with strong light-matter interactions to boost the dehydrogenation of chemical hydrogen carriers.

10.1021/acs.inorgchem.6c04345.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrite (NO2–) reduction to hydroxylamine (NH2OH) under ambient conditions is regarded as a sustainable way to simultaneously enable pollutant abatement and value-added chemical synthesis; however, the intrinsically sluggish kinetics and competing over-reduction to ammonia necessitate the rational exploration of robust electrocatalytic systems. Herein, we report the anchoring of zinc phthalocyanine (ZnPc) molecules onto bamboo-like nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes encapsulating metallic cobalt nanoparticles (Co-NCNT) for selectively converting NO2– to NH2OH. The resulting ZnPc/Co-NCNT electrocatalyst achieves a considerable NH2OH yield of 0.25 mmol h–1 mgcat–1 and a high Faradaic efficiency of 64.32% at −0.3 V vs RHE, significantly outperforming its monocomponent counterparts. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co-NCNT facilitates charge transfer and lowers the water dissociation barrier, securing efficient active hydrogen (*H) supply to drive the hydrogenation processes. Furthermore, the practical viability of this system is demonstrated by constructing a Zn–NO2– battery, which concurrently generates NH2OH while delivering a peak power density of 7.22 mW cm–2. This study underscores the efficacy of synergistically integrating molecular catalysts with functional carriers for selective NO2– electroreduction to NH2OH.

10.1021/acs.jchemed.6c01163.abstract: Abstract Ammonia borane (NH3BH3, AB) is a chemical hydrogen storage material with high hydrogen content, low molecular weight, and good stability. Herein, an undergraduate laboratory experiment was designed for students in materials science, chemical engineering, energy science, and related disciplines to demonstrate H2 production from AB hydrolysis and its application. A Pd/C nanocomposite was employed as a catalyst in the experiment that integrates kinetic analysis with practical utilization. Students first recorded H2-production curves and determined key parameters of turnover frequency and activation energy and then used the generated H2 to power a small fuel-cell car. The entire experiment was completed within approximately 4 h. Through this experiment, students may develop essential experimental skills and gain a systematic understanding of H2 generation from AB hydrolysis and its applications.

10.1021/acs.jpclett.6c03171.abstract: Abstract Ambient ammonia synthesis is important for carbon neutrality. Tribo-electro-catalysis, which converts mechanical friction into chemical driving force through contact electrification and charge transfer, offers a route for nitrogen (N2) fixation. However, inefficient utilization of friction-induced charges and insufficient N2 activation remain major challenges. Herein, acid-etching defect engineering regulates the surface and electronic structures of lead telluride (PbTe) for N2 fixation. The catalyst etched for 90 min exhibits the enhanced activity under dark ambient conditions, delivering ammonium (NH4+) production rates of 258.98 and 329.60 μmol L–1·g–1·h–1 without and with 10 vol % methanol, respectively. Analyses reveal that etching reconstructs the surface, generates defect sites, facilitates N2 adsorption and activation, and promotes friction-induced charge utilization. Excessive etching decreases activity. Charge-trapping and electron paramagnetic resonance measurements support the role of friction-induced negative charges, establishing defect-mediated charge regulation as an effective strategy for sustainable ammonia synthesis.

10.1021/acsami.6c16760.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3RR) represents a promising strategy for sustainable ammonia synthesis while simultaneously addressing nitrate pollution in wastewater. However, the irreversible structural reconstruction commonly observed in catalysts during NO3RR obscures the true active sites and complicates mechanistic understanding. In this study, flower-like CuCo2S4 nanocrystals synthesized via a hot-injection method serve as a model ternary sulfide system to systematically probe reconstruction dynamics and identify active phases under operating conditions. Experimental characterizations reveal that CuCo2S4 gradually evolves into Cu-Co(OH)2/Co9S8 through electrochemical reconstruction. This reconstructed catalyst exhibits excellent NO3RR performance, achieving an average Faradaic efficiency of 97.3%, an ammonia production rate of 363.1 μmol h–1 mg–1, and remarkable cycling stability. In situ FTIR spectra indicate that Cu incorporation promotes the conversion of *NO2 and accelerates subsequent hydrogenation steps. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that Cu doping facilitates *NH3 desorption and optimizes the balance between NO3– adsorption and *NH3 release. This work systematically deciphers the reconstruction pathway of sulfide catalysts during NO3RR, offering fundamental insights into electrocatalyst reconstruction mechanisms and providing a design strategy for high-performance ammonia-production electrocatalysts.

10.1021/acsami.6c18993.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has emerged as a sustainable circular-economy approach that enables simultaneous remediation of nitrate-contaminated wastewater and green ammonia synthesis. However, practical implementation of NO3RR is severely hindered by complicated multi-proton-electron transfer processes, undesirable nitrite accumulation, and competing hydrogen evolution reactions. While bimetallic heterostructured tandem catalysts hold great potential to address these issues, conventional spatially separated dual-site configurations still suffer from sluggish intermediate relay, mismatched reaction kinetics, and uncontrollable nitrite desorption. Heterointerfaces modulate intermediate (*NO3, *NO2, *H) adsorption and boost in situ active-hydrogen production to match cascade reaction kinetics. Combined operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the heterointerface efficiently suppresses excessive *NO2 desorption, strengthens nitrite intermediate trapping, and enriches surface-active hydrogen species, resolving the kinetic mismatch that plagues traditional dual-site catalytic systems. This work establishes an interface-dominated pathway for the design of high-efficiency intrinsic tandem catalysts, breaking through the performance bottleneck of conventional simple phase-mixing strategies.

Mechanistic investigations suggest that CuO-1 undergoes partial reduction during the reaction to generate Cu0/Cu+ species, which may serve as key active species promoting ammonia production by enhancing active hydrogen generation. Finally, NH4Cl was recovered through acid absorption and rotary evaporation, demonstrating a practical route for converting NO3− pollutants into valuable NH3 products.

10.1021/acsanm.6c05096.abstract: Abstract Ammonia (NH3) is a representative reducing toxic gas whose rapid, low-concentration detection is important in constant-temperature, constant-humidity environments such as semiconductor cleanrooms, yet existing NH3 sensors often suffer from high operating temperatures or slow response/recovery kinetics. Fibrous phosphorus (FP), a layered allotrope of elemental phosphorus with a parallel tubular structure, is an appealing sensing candidate, but its efficient preparation and gas-sensing potential remain underexplored. Here, we report an iodine-assisted chemical vapor transport method that enables gram-scale synthesis of FP within 5 h with a yield exceeding 99%, without the need for precise temperature-gradient control. The key is the iodine-mediated cleavage of P4 cages and the directed assembly of active phosphorus fragments into tubular FP. Taking advantage of the weak interlayer van der Waals interactions, high-quality FP nanoribbons (FP-NRs) with an average width of ∼50 nm, an average length of ∼6 μm, and aspect ratios exceeding 150 for ∼60% of the ribbons are obtained by 60 min of ice-bath exfoliation. The FP-NRs sensor exhibits a high response of 826% toward 100 ppm NH3 at room temperature, with response/recovery times of 31/7 s under the 90% criterion, and remains responsive at 2 ppm NH3 (response 69.8%). When all tested gases are compared at the same concentration, the response to NH3 is significantly higher than that to the interfering gases. Combined DFT calculations and in situ FTIR/Raman measurements reveal that NH3 adsorption on FP is dominated by physical adsorption (adsorption energy −0.26 eV; Bader charge transfer ∼0.02 e), which accounts for the high sensitivity, selectivity, and fast recovery. This work provides a scalable route to FP nanoribbons and demonstrates their potential for practical room-temperature NH3 sensing.

10.1021/acsapm.6c04260.abstract: Abstract Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), a synthetic thermoplastic polymer, has been extensively used in our lives due to its advantageous properties such as high transparency, lightweight, and biocompatibility. Although PMMA exhibits great potential in sunscreens, its poor UV-blocking properties hinder its practical applications. In this study, we modified the PMMA submicron spheres (120–150 nm) with nanoscale ZnO using atomic layer deposition (ALD) in a fluidized bed reactor at a low temperature of 40 °C, with diethylzinc (DEZ) and water as precursors. We systematically investigated the ZnO-coated PMMA microspheres using FTIR, XRD, SEM, TEM, XPS, and TG to elucidate the mechanism of nucleation and growth of ZnO. The results revealed that the ZnO deposited was polycrystalline, displaying a granular morphology on the PMMA surfaces. Specifically, a nanoparticle-coated structure was observed after low-cycle ALD, while a conformal nanofilm was formed after high-cycle ALD on the PMMA spheres, suggesting an island growth mode of ZnO. The analysis of the surface chemical species and functional groups via XPS and in situ FTIR indicated that the fast nucleation of ZnO was attributed to trace amounts of hydroxyl groups and hydrogen-bonded water molecules bound on the surfaces of the emulsion-polymerized submicron PMMA spheres. After ZnO coating, the PMMA microspheres exhibited improved UV-blocking performance. The reflectance within the 280–400 nm UV range dropped sharply from ca. 95% (pristine PMMA) to 19% for the PMMA/ZnO composite which had an optical bandgap of 3.36 eV. Meanwhile, the average visible-light reflectance remained above 93%. Moreover, owing to the physical barrier effect of the ZnO coating, the derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) peak temperature increased by 30 °C and the acetone resistance improved. This study not only provides a feasible strategy for modifying polymeric particle surfaces and fabricating organic–inorganic hybrid materials but could also advance the uses of PMMA spheres in high-end cosmetics.

10.1021/acscatal.6c04945.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (e-NO3– RR) to ammonia offers an effective pathway for environmental remediation and clean energy production. However, its efficiency is often constrained by sluggish multi-electron/proton transfer and mismatched intermediate adsorption. Herein, we report a bioinspired multi-metallic cobalt copper molybdate (CCM) catalyst that overcomes these limitations through a relay-type catalytic mechanism enabled by spatially distinct metal centers. In this architecture, Cu, Co, and Mo sites cooperatively orchestrate intermediate stabilization and proton activation in successive reaction steps, thereby facilitating an efficient cascade conversion of nitrate to ammonia. As a result, the optimized CCM catalyst achieves an ammonia yield rate of 2.6 mmol h–1 cm–2 and a Faradaic efficiency up to 92%. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses identify the synergistic interplay among the multiple metal active centers as the mechanistic basis for the enhanced nitrate-to-ammonia performance. Beyond half-cell evaluation, integration of the CCM catalyst into a Zn-NO3– battery delivers an output voltage of 1.34 V and a power density of 4.1 mW cm–2, demonstrating its viability for coupled ammonia synthesis and energy generation. This study identifies multi-metallic relay catalysis as an effective strategy for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate-to-ammonia conversion.

10.1021/acscatal.6c07178.abstract: Abstract The development of high-efficiency NH3 synthesis catalysts under mild conditions is urgently required to alleviate the excessive energy consumption and carbon emissions in traditional Haber–Bosch processes. Although Ru-based catalysts show considerable potential, their catalytic activity is often severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning caused by strong H2 adsorption. Herein, we report the fabrication of a Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst through the strategic integration of single-atom Re species into a conventional Ba/Ru/AC framework. Notably, the Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst exhibits a high NH3 synthesis rate of 65.1 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa. Mechanistic investigations reveal that single-atom Re species function as a supplementary active site for H2 adsorption and activation. The incorporation of Re also facilitates H-spillover over the catalyst surface, which effectively alleviates the competitive adsorption between H2 and N2 on Ru sites and consequently mitigates hydrogen poisoning on Ru nanoclusters. Concurrently, the incorporation of single-atom Re modulates the defect density of the support and promotes the creation of additional strong Lewis basic sites. These structural changes induce a strong electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) effect, which specifically tunes the electronic structure of the Ru nanoclusters. This synergistic interplay between single-atom Re sites and Ru nanoclusters establishes a compelling paradigm for the rational design of highly efficient NH3 synthesis catalysts.

10.1021/acsenergylett.6c02646.abstract: Abstract Lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction (LiNRR) produces ammonia at ambient pressure and temperature, and gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) have advanced its production rate by intensifying nitrogen availability. However, the mass transport of lithium, nitrogen, and proton donor within the GDE and how the balance of their fluxes governs LiNRR performance remain underexplored. Here, we spatiotemporally varied the balance of species fluxes in a LiNRR GDE by dynamically modulating the pressure difference across the electrode, which altered the position of the gas/electrolyte interface. We found that decoupling the pressures applied during the plating and resting steps of pulsed electrolysis leads to higher ammonia production rates compared to the corresponding static pressure conditions. Decoupled pressure modulation enables even lithium plating during electrolysis and fast transport of nitrogen and proton donor during subsequent ammonia formation steps. This strategy may unlock a new design space for LiNRR by dynamically optimizing the reaction interface.

10.1021/acsestwater.6c01131.abstract: Abstract Predicting the ammonium nitrogen (NH4+-N) adsorption capacity of biochar is challenged by coupled, nonlinear interactions among operational variables, pyrolysis synthesis parameters, and intrinsic material properties. A unified data set comprising 425 literature-reported adsorption records from 18 studies was compiled, and preprocessing (KNN imputation and Z-score standardization) was fitted exclusively on the training subset to prevent data leakage. Among seven machine learning algorithms benchmarked with Bayesian optimization and 5-fold cross-validation, XGBoost achieved the highest test-set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.901 and root-mean-square error of 0.555 mg g–1. TreeSHAP analysis quantitatively decoupled three driver groups, adsorption operational parameters (53.3%), biochar physicochemical properties (38.2%), and pyrolysis synthesis parameters (8.5%), and identified initial concentration, biochar oxygen content, and adsorbent dosage as the dominant variables, with oxygen content exhibiting a unimodal relationship with adsorption capacity. Partial dependence plots were further utilized to reveal nonlinear response behaviors and determine data-coverage-validated optimal operation and design windows for key variables. A graphical user interface was developed to estimate equilibrium adsorption capacity, reducing reliance on extensive laboratory trials.

10.1021/acssensors.6c04300.abstract: Abstract Atomically dispersed noble-metal sensitizers offer an effective means of enhancing semiconductor metal oxide gas sensors, yet a single type of atomic noble-metal site is often insufficient to optimize both gas adsorption and catalytic oxidation. Here, atomically dispersed Pt and Pd sites are co-engineered on mesoporous SnO2 nanospheres to establish a cascade adsorption–oxidation pathway for enhanced NH3 sensing. The Pt/Pd–SnO2 sensor exhibits 4.1-, 6.2-, and 26-fold higher NH3 sensitivity than Pt–SnO2, Pd–SnO2, and mesoporous SnO2, respectively, with a calculated detection limit of 100 ppb and a response time of approximately 2 s. In situ spectroscopy, temperature-programmed desorption, and density functional theory calculations reveal that Pd-associated defect motifs promote the adsorption of NH3 and O2, whereas Pt–O–Sn motifs facilitate the subsequent oxidation of adsorbed NH3-derived species. The coexistence of atomically dispersed Pt and Pd dual-sensitizers therefore couples enhanced adsorption with accelerated catalytic oxidation, providing an atomic-scale noble-metal engineering strategy for high-performance gas sensing.

10.1021/acssuschemeng.6c03827.abstract: Abstract Ammonia synthesis based on steam methane reforming (SMR) is characterized by intensive energy consumption and high carbon emissions. To address these limitations, novel processes integrating gasification and carbon capture technologies were proposed for converting waste tires into blue ammonia. Detailed safety, techno-economic, and life cycle assessments were conducted to evaluate comprehensive performance. Machine learning-driven multiobjective operation optimization was carried out for reducing levelized cost of ammonia (LCOA) while enhancing safety and sustainability scores based on safe-and-sustainable-by-design framework. Our results highlight the critical role of artificial neural networks in achieving efficient optimization. Additionally, the quantitative impacts of integrating various renewable energy sources were investigated. The results showed the conventional gasification (CG) integrating methyldiethanolamine (MDEA)-based carbon capture alternative achieved the optimal LCOA at 358.1 $/ton in current electricity scenario. A peak environmental sustainability score of 0.443 was achieved, outperforming traditional SMR integrating MDEA-based carbon capture pathway by 13.04%. The safest process is CG integrating monoethanolamine-based carbon capture. 10.1021/acssuschemeng.6c07588.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NitRR) offers a sustainable route for nitrate removal and ammonia production, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish multistep kinetics and competitive hydrogen evolution. Herein, a CuSA–ZnO@CW electrocatalyst was constructed by stabilizing O–coordinated Cu single atoms on defective ZnO supported by carbonized wood. The conductive wood-derived scaffold facilitates mass/electron transport, while the defective ZnO/Cu–O3 interface regulates local adsorption competition between NO3– and H2O. CuSA–ZnO@CW delivers an NH3 yield of 3561.9 μg h–1 cm–2 and a Faradaic efficiency of 97.07% at –1.1 V vs RHE, with stable performance over 36 cycles. Mechanistic studies reveal that ZnO preferentially accommodates interfacial H2O, whereas Cu–O3 sites selectively activate NO3– and promote NOX intermediate conversion, thereby reducing the free-energy requirement of the potential-determining step and suppressing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This work presents a defective oxide–regulated single–atom interface for selective NO3– to NH3 conversion.

10.1021/acssuschemeng.6c09970.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic ammonia oxidation (AOR) offers an energy-efficient route to carbon-free hydrogen production but is constrained by sluggish multielectron-transfer kinetics and adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) scaling relationships. Here, electrodeposition yielded a nickel-foam-supported bimetallic FeCuN catalyst (FeCuN-BH), followed by high-temperature hydrogenation to introduce abundant lattice nitrogen vacancies (FeCuN-AH). The rationally engineered FeCuN-AH architecture demonstrates superior AOR performance, requiring an exceptionally low applied potential of 0.61 V vs the saturated calomel electrode (SCE) to reach 50 mA cm–2, together with an apparent Tafel slope of 934.7 mV dec–1, substantially lower than the 2408 mV dec–1 measured for FeCuN-BH, and stable operation over 50 h. Comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate a lattice nitrogen vacancy-mediated dual-site synergistic mechanism (LNVM-MSM). The incorporated nitrogen vacancies not only serve as preferential active centers for ammonia adsorption but also drastically reduce the kinetic energy barrier of the rate-determining step (RDS, *NH2 to *NH) from 2.04 eV on pristine copper sites down to 0.90 eV. Furthermore, these defect sites induce local electronic redistribution and modify intermediate adsorption energetics. By circumventing conventional scaling limitations, this defect-driven dual-site structure provides a robust and scalable framework for designing active, durable electrocatalysts for sustainable hydrogen extraction and advanced energy-conversion devices.

10.1021/jacs.6c14152.abstract: Abstract Plasmonic photocatalysis can enhance conventional chemical transformations, but macroscale kinetic metrics, such as overall reaction rates and apparent activation barriers, are insufficient to identify the specific elementary steps modulated by hot carriers, limiting precise control over catalytic reactivity and selectivity. Here, we apply a spectrokinetic strategy based on in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) to resolve elementary-step energetics in NH3 decomposition over CuRu alloy antenna–reactor catalysts. CuRu and Na-modified CuRu show different relative sensitivities to heating and illumination, providing a paired system for tracking how kinetic control is redistributed under thermal and plasmonic conditions. Temporal in situ DRIFTS and Arrhenius analysis identify site-dependent adsorbed N2 (*N2) intermediates and reveal a sequential migration–desorption pathway for *N2 removal. Thermal kinetic analysis shows that Na enhances thermocatalytic activity, despite strengthening *N2 binding and increasing the *N2 desorption barrier at terrace sites, while DFT calculations suggest that this enhancement is consistent with a reduced interfacial N–N coupling barrier. Under illumination, CuRu exhibits a nearly three-orders-of-magnitude light-specific rate enhancement, accompanied by decreases of 0.75 and 0.28 eV in the activation barriers for terrace *N2 desorption and interfacial *N2 migration, respectively, relative to dark thermal conditions. Comparing CuRu and CuRu–Na shows that illumination affects interfacial *N2 migration more selectively than terrace *N2 desorption, identifying interfacial *N2 removal as a site-sensitive step in plasmon-promoted active-site regeneration. These findings connect plasmonic excitation with site-dependent surface dynamics and elementary-step energetics, providing a framework for understanding how light redirects kinetic control in multistep catalysis.

10.1021/jacs.6c14894.abstract: Abstract The electroreduction of nitrogen oxides offers a promising route for green synthesis of hydroxylamine (NH2OH). Although Pd exhibited high selectivity toward NH2OH production experimentally, we found the dominant hollow sites of pristine Pd prefer ammonia production via the NOH*-pathway. This discrepancy was resolved by unveiling the critical roles of in situ hydriding of Pd under operando conditions. Using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations driven by machine learning potential, we demonstrated the potential-dependent structural evolution from pristine Pd to palladium hydride (PdHx) under −0.11 to −0.51 V vs RHE. For the in situ-generated PdHx surfaces with some amorphous or disordering features, the dominant hollow sites of Pd are blocked by adsorbed H* species, thereby repelling NO* to adsorb obliquely on PdHx top sites. The adsorption configuration of NO* steers the reaction pathway from NOH* to HNO* formation, leading to NH2OH* production eventually. In addition, the PdHx top sites exhibit generally downshifted d-band centers, promoting NH2OH* desorption and preventing its over-reduction to ammonia. At last, a site sensitivity was proposed for hydroxylamine electrosynthesis based on the analysis on a variety of catalysts; the formation energies of HNO* vs NOH* and the adsorption energy of NH2OH* were identified as important features resulting in high hydroxylamine selectivity.

10.1021/jacs.6c15718.abstract: Abstract Above 0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, the hydrogen evolution reaction is thermodynamically suppressed, making this potential region attractive for nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. However, in neutral and alkaline media typically used for the nitrate reduction reaction, protons for successive hydrogenation steps derive mainly from water dissociation, which becomes increasingly sluggish at more positive potentials. Proton availability thus governs the hydrogenation kinetics of nitrate and its intermediates. Using CuRu nanorods as a model catalyst, we resolve how the electrolyte and the catalyst jointly control the proton supply during NO3RR at positive potentials. Macroelectrode measurements reveal that the NO3– reduction kinetics depend on OH– concentration, and single-particle electrochemistry on a single CuRu nanorod, where ultrafast mass transport avoids local OH– accumulation, assigns this dependence to the bulk. Moreover, in situ scanning electrochemical microscopy shows that bulk OH– governs water dissociation kinetics; capacitance and potential-of-zero-charge measurements trace this to a strengthened, cation-enriched interfacial electric field, which accelerates water dissociation and sustains the proton supply at positive potentials. Building on the electrolyte-enhanced proton supply, Cu incorporation tunes the competitive adsorption between H2O-derived species and NO3– on the CuRu surface, thereby avoiding a proton oversupply that compromises the conversion kinetics. These results provide systematic insight into how bulk OH– concentration and catalyst composition cooperatively modulate proton supply, enhancing nitrate-to-ammonia conversion at HER-free potentials.

10.1021/jacs.6c16282.abstract: Abstract The electrolyte and applied potential are known to impact a catalyst’s structure and performance, yet the role of reaction intermediates and products in driving surface evolution remains largely unexplored. Here, using electrochemical atomic force microscopy, we show that the dynamic restructuring of copper (Cu) surfaces during nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) directly correlates with the rate and selectivity of ammonia (NH3) formation. At moderate overpotentials, where nitrite formation dominates, lateral expansion of Cu terraces is observed, whereas rapid NH3 formation at higher cathodic potentials induces Cu adislands enriched in low-coordinated step sites, revealing distinct restructuring pathways that accompany the transition from nitrite- to ammonia-selective NO3RR. These transformations are rationalized by an NH3-mediated Cu dissolution-redeposition mechanism. Our results identify reaction products as active modulators of catalyst surface structure, establishing a framework for understanding reaction-driven catalyst restructuring and enabling in situ control of catalyst surfaces through the interfacial reaction environment.

10.1021/jacs.6c16802.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish N–O bond cleavage, incomplete NOx hydrogenation, and competing hydrogen evolution reaction. However, how catalyst structural engineering regulates the interfacial microenvironment remains unclear, despite its critical importance for constructing efficient catalysts. Here, we report a Cu3Ru7 catalyst with abundant Cu–Ru interfaces, where interface-induced water reorganization enables efficient NH3 production. The Cu3Ru7 catalyst exhibits an impressive NH3 formation rate of 19.7 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 5 A cm–2 in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer and remains stable at 2 A cm–2 with an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of ∼86% for 500 h. A scale-up demonstration using a 100 cm2 MEA electrolyzer affords an NH3 formation rate up to 1.5 mol h–1 at 400 A. The in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that Cu3Ru7 catalyst establishes a moderate interfacial hydrogen-bond network, which creates a water-mediated interfacial micro environment that facilitates NOx deoxygenation and subsequent NHx formation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations further reveal that the Cu–Ru interface stabilizes the dissociating oxygen atom through a persistent and dynamically connected hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating sequential NO3– → NO2 → NO conversion. Meanwhile, the surrounding Cu matrix attenuates the excessive *H accumulation characteristic of Ru, suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes Cu–Ru interface-induced interfacial water reorganization as a strategy for improving electrocatalytic nitrate reduction performance.

10.1021/photonsci.6c00065.abstract: Abstract This work presents the design, implementation, and validation of a custom-built in situ atomic layer deposition (ALD) reactor developed at the ALBA Synchrotron Light Source (Cerdanyola del Vallès, Spain), enabling direct integration with synchrotron X-ray beamlines. A modular configuration allows the ALD reactor to be deployed at two ALBA Synchrotron beamlines: NCD-SWEET beamline (BL11) for Grazing Incidence Small Angle X-ray Scattering (GISAXS) and NOTOS beamline (BL16) for X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), requiring only minimal reconfiguration. The reactor performance was validated by in situ deposition of TiO2 thin films using titanium tetraisopropoxide (TTIP) and H2O as the precursor and co-reactant, respectively, with a growth per cycle (GPC) of 0.17 Å·cycle–1 at 150 °C. This system was chosen for its low growth rate, as a demanding test of detection sensitivity. In situ GISAXS revealed the continuous evolution of film morphology and near-surface electron density over 1000 ALD cycles, while in situ X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) quantitatively resolved three kinetically distinct growth regimes: prenucleation, nucleation development, and steady-state growth. The complementarity of the two techniques provides a comprehensive picture of ALD growth dynamics that neither technique could deliver independently, demonstrating the potential of the ALD system presented here for in situ multi-technique characterization of a broad range of ALD processes.

10.1080/00103624.2026.2762883.abstract: Despite its importance as a climate-resilient nutri-cereal, little millet has received limited attention with respect to nitrogen management and nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) studies. Excessive reliance on inorganic fertilizers often leads to poor nitrogen utilization, whereas integrated application of organic and inorganic nitrogen sources may improve nitrogen uptake and crop productivity. Therefore, a field experiment was conducted during the kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 at the Research Farm of Advanced Center for Rainfed Agriculture, Rakh Dhiansar, Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Jammu to evaluate the effect of cultivars and nitrogen management practices on growth, yield, nitrogen uptake and NUE of little millet. The experiment was laid out in randomized complete block design with factorial arrangement and replicated thrice, comprising three cultivars and six nitrogen treatments. Among cultivars, BL 6 (V2) recorded significantly higher growth parameters, yield attributes, grain yield, straw yield, nitrogen uptake and NUE over GPUL 6 (V1) and the local variety (V3). Among nitrogen treatments, integrated application of 10 kg ha−1 N through farmyard manure (FYM) + 30 kg ha−1 N through urea (N6) recorded significantly higher growth, yield attributes, grain yield, straw yield, nitrogen uptake, agronomic efficiency and recovery efficiency than all other treatments except 40 kg ha−1 N through urea (N2), with which it was statistically at par. However, N2 recorded the highest benefit-cost ratio. Simple linear regression revealed positive relationships of grain yield with grains per panicle (R2 = 0.99) and total nitrogen uptake (R2 = 0.93) showing the highest coefficients of determination. The results indicated that integrated application of FYM and urea improved nitrogen uptake and NUE while sustaining productivity of little millet.

10.1080/00219592.2026.2750603.abstract: Constrained Bayesian optimization (BO) is a promising approach for optimizing chemical processes under limited evaluation budgets. In this study, BO was applied to an ammonia production process, and three surrogate models—Gaussian process regression (GPR), random forest (RF), and Bayesian linear regression (BLR)—were systematically compared. GPR achieved the highest optimization performance in terms of best-observed profit, whereas RF provided superior robustness with consistent identification of feasible solutions. BLR showed balanced performance with lower computational cost. Sensitivity analysis revealed that system behavior is governed by a small subset of variables, indicating low effective dimensionality. This structural property explains the strong performance of GPR. In addition, the relative performance of surrogate models was found to depend on economic conditions and optimization settings, as changes in dominant variables altered model suitability. Quantitatively, GPR achieved an average best-observed profit 10.4% and 5.2% higher than RF and BLR, respectively; RF identified 40.3% more feasible solutions than GPR; and BLR required only approximately 1/13 and 1/319 of the BO computation times required by GPR and RF, respectively. These results suggest that surrogate model selection in constrained BO should be adapted to problem structure and computational requirements, rather than relying on a single model.

10.1080/09593330.2026.2759892.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction offers a promising route for removing nitrate contaminants from water while recovering nitrogen as ammonia, but its practical efficiency is limited by sluggish nitrate activation and competing hydrogen evolution. Herein, we report a strong metal–support interaction-engineered Cu/LaOx catalyst for selective nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. The optimized Cu/LaOx interface was constructed by regulating the Cu/LaOx ratio, where LaOx partially encapsulates Cu sites and induces interfacial La–O–Cu bonding, oxygen vacancies, and electronic redistribution around Cu centres. These interfacial features enhance nitrate adsorption, accelerate deoxygenation, and facilitate subsequent hydrogenation steps. As a result, the optimized 1:1Cu/LaOx-3DOMC catalyst achieves a high ammonia yield rate of 0.8961 mmol h−1 cm−2 and a Faradaic efficiency of 94.5% at −0.64 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, markedly outperforming the LaOx-free Cu catalyst. Electrochemical analysis further reveal enhanced nitrate reduction current response, increased electrochemically active surface area, and reduced charge-transfer resistance. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations confirm that Cu/LaOx interfacial coupling promotes *H-assisted nitrate deoxygenation and *NO hydrogenation while suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. This work demonstrates that strong metal–support interaction engineering is an effective strategy for coupling electrocatalytic nitrate removal with nitrogen resource recovery from contaminated water.

10.1080/29984475.2026.2748636.abstract: The increasing need for academic literacy provision in higher education has led to discussion around how discipline-specific language can be embedded into curricula. While the Academic Literacies approach is commonly referenced in these discussions, few frameworks have been proposed regarding processes and roles involved in embedding initiatives. This qualitative research synthesis unveils the processes and roles reported in recent embedding initiatives, revealing a trend of EAP staff’s starting in the middle of the teaching cycle and the common practice of academic literacy provision being based around assessments. This leads to issues within the embedding process, especially surrounding the identification of discipline-specific literacies, their embedding into curricula and their teaching alongside content. The impact of the failure to consider academic literacies at curriculum design stage is examined, before a more robust embedding model is proposed. The Identify, Design, Teach (IDT) model promotes the embedding of EAP staff into faculties as well as their involvement in curriculum and assessment design, leading to the successful identification of discipline-specific literacies and their embedding into subject curricula and assessment. The benefits of the IDT model include the constructive alignment between learning objectives, teaching materials and assessments as well as academic literacy provision that helps students to engage with subject content.

10.1117/12.3123214.abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) TiO₂ thin films are widely used in optoelectronics, photocatalysis, and biomedical applications. However, their intrinsic absorption and defect-induced absorption limit their application in high-power laser optics. Annealing is an important post-treatment method to modulate the optical properties and reduce absorption. In this work, ALD-TiO₂ thin films were annealed in O₂ atmosphere at different temperatures. The effects of annealing temperature on the optical constants, surface morphology, crystal structure, and impurity states were systematically investigated using spectroscopic ellipsometry, atomic force microscopy (AFM), X-ray diffraction(XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy(FTIR), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). This work provides theoretical and experimental guidance for the preparation of low-absorption, high laser-damage-resistant ALD-TiO₂ optical films through post-annealing treatment.

10.1149/1945-7111/aebcb9.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic reduction reaction of nitrate to ammonia (NO3RR) has emerged as a promising strategy that couples nitrate pollutant remediation with sustainable NH3 production. Practical nitrate-containing industrial wastewater usually presents a wide pH distribution range, which puts forward an urgent requirement for pH-adaptive NO₃RR catalysts with high ammonia selectivity. Conventional NO3RR catalysts fail to deliver high NH3 Faradaic efficiency under extreme acidic or alkaline conditions, mainly due to uncontrollable competitive adsorption of hydrogen intermediates on active sites. Herein, we report a ruthenium-decorated copper foam catalyst (RuCuF@PUS) fabricated via a facile two-step electrodeposition method, which achieves exceptional NO3RR performance across a wide pH window of 1-12. The interconnected porous framework enables efficient mass transfer, while the precisely designed dual active sites endow Cu with strong nitrate adsorption and activation capability, and Ru with accelerated sequential hydrogenation kinetics. In acidic condition, the catalyst achieves a remarkable ammonia yield rate of 457.56 µmol/h·cm2 at −0.4 V vs. RHE, with a peak Faradaic efficiency of 90.96%. Furthermore, a proof-of-concept alkaline-acidic hybrid Zn–NO3 battery assembled with the RuCuF@PUS cathode and real nitrate-containing wastewater as electrolyte achieves an open-circuit voltage of 1.29 V and a peak power density of 25.93 mW/cm2.

10.17185/duepublico/88455.abstract: The electrochemical nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) offers a sustainable route to ammonia synthesis under ambient conditions; however, its practical realization is fundamentally limited by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which dominates under the same cathodic potential window. Molybdenum-based MXenes have emerged as a promising catalyst class due to their tunable surface chemistry and intrinsic electronic flexibility, yet a mechanistic understanding of how NRR and HER compete on these surfaces has remained incomplete. This thesis addresses this challenge using a density functional theory (DFT) framework to resolve catalytic behavior under electrochemical conditions and to identify the fundamental origin of selectivity. The work is structured around four complementary strategies for modulating the surface structure and chemistry of Mo-based MXenes to control the competition between the NRR and the HER. Two strategies involve chemical surface engineering through nitrogen- and fluorine-containing terminations, one exploits lattice strain, and the fourth employs potential-induced surface reconstruction. First, chemical modulation reveals that introducing a nitrogen-rich environment around the active site — experimentally accessible via molten-salt synthesis — enhances nitrogen activation while suppressing hydrogen adsorption, thereby reversing the catalytic selectivity from HER-dominated to NRR-dominated. Second, mixed *F/*O/*OH surface configurations arising from HF-based MXene synthesis are systematically investigated, demonstrating that variations in surface composition strongly influence catalytic behavior, with mixed fluorine-, oxygen-, and hydroxyl-terminated surfaces providing the most favorable balance between NRR activity and HER suppression. Third, strain engineering tunes the electronic structure of Mo2C(0001): tensile strain stabilizes nitrogen adsorption and promotes NRR, whereas compressive strain enhances hydrogen adsorption and favors HER, with the work function emerging as a robust descriptor to rationalize these trends. Fourth, moving beyond static modifications, potential-induced surface reconstruction demonstrates that molybdenum-based MXenes can form single-atom-like centers under anodic polarization. Upon applying a subsequent cathodic potential pulse, these in-situ-generated sites become catalytically active and steer the reaction selectively toward ammonia formation — a dynamic modulation strategy fundamentally distinct from the previous three. To ensure that these trends are described on a consistent thermodynamic basis, the accuracy of the underlying free-energy landscape is further examined. Standard DFT introduces systematic errors in the treatment of gas-phase reference molecules such as N2, H2, and NH3; these propagate across the entire reaction network. A statistical gas-phase correction framework is therefore developed that goes beyond the standard implementation in the community, advancing thermodynamically consistent free-energy diagrams and improving the reliability of activity descriptors and selectivity predictions. This thesis demonstrates that selectivity on Mo-based MXene surfaces sensitively depends on surface coverage, active sites, and potential-dependent changes in the surface structure. The findings provide a unified thermodynamic framework for evaluating NRR–HER competition, identify stable surface terminations under operating conditions, and derive electronic design principles linking termination chemistry, strain, and reconstruction to catalytic performance. The methodologies developed here are transferable to other electrocatalytic systems and offer a foundation for sustainable catalyst design across a range of energy-relevant reactions.

10.2118/235635-ms.abstract: Abstract Green ammonia projects face increasing challenges in progressing from conceptual development toward bankable execution, requiring coordinated development across technology, infrastructure, safety assurance, and commercial pathways. This paper presents the outcome of an ongoing front-end development program for a compact floating green ammonia FPSO-type facility. It discusses how mature technologies can be selected for floating applications, modularized, marinized, and integrated with safety-led design to support a scalable and bankable infrastructure model. The development incorporates contributions from the project developer, the design and fabrication contractor, and an independent classification and technical assurance partner. Market-driven design considerations include renewable power availability, geographical location, export route, and potential offtake markets. The technical scope includes approximately 500 MW renewable power intake, high-voltage distribution, hydrogen production, nitrogen generation, ammonia synthesis, refrigerated storage, utilities, marine systems, and offloading interfaces. Safety studies comprise HAZID, layout review, safety screening, and coarse quantitative risk assessment covering hydrogen and ammonia major accident hazards, including hydrogen accumulation and explosion risk, ammonia toxic dispersion, compact layout constraints, marine offloading interfaces, and nearshore risk exposure. The paper demonstrates how technical readiness, commercial readiness, and safety and regulatory readiness can be matured together to progress the concept beyond Approval in Principle toward an execution-ready project definition.

10.2118/235870-ms.abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are flammable and some of them are hazardous to human health. Apart from its toxic nature, VOCs can also take part into photochemical reactions and contribute to formation of ozone and fine particles, causing detrimental influences on atmospheric quality. Increase in VOCs emission from human activity has been recognized as primary causes of urban air pollution in China, and targeted control and constant removal of VOCs was proposed as key measures to mitigate atmosphere problems. Petrochemical facility was significant emission sources for VOCs and NOx and represents an possibility of co-treatment of these two pollutants. In this work, treatment of petrochemical VOCs by directing VOCs stream into facility heater or process furnace was proposed and confirmed. The oxidation of VOCs and its influence on NOx conversion was probed within an experimental setup, simulating the co-conversion process of petrochemical VOCs and NOx. The propane and propylene were selected as representatives of petrochemical VOCs and used as reactant with a feed ratio of 2% and 0.5% (V/V %). NO was chosen to act as NOx at feeding concentration of 200 and 800 mg/m3. Air stream was also feed to simulate oxidative condition within the process furnace or incinerator. Influences of VOCs species, temperature and concentration on NOx conversion were confirmed. The results suggest that reduction of NO takes place in the presence of VOCs at temperature higher than 300°C regardless of NO concentration. The VOCs species selectively reduce NO below 500°C while it was gradually oxidized by oxygen as temperature further increases and was completely consumed above 700°C. Lower temperature favors NO reduction by VOCs compared with high temperature (above 600°C). An optimum temperature window (400~600°C) was obtained for NO conversion by VOCs and more than 30% NO can be reduced by VOCs. Concentration of VOCs also play an important role in NO reduction. Increase in ratio of VOCs facilitate NO reduction. Alkane seems to be more reactive in NO reduction than alkene. According to finding in this work, it was advised that the alkane VOCs stream was routed into latter stage of process furnace with temperature lower than 700°C where NOx has been formed. In case of alkene and aromatic VOCs stream, a higher temperature was needed and the former furnace stage was more preferred. In the first time, co-treatment of VOCs and NOx in petrochemical facility was proposed. The feasibility and performance were subsequently confirmed in lab scale setup. The information obtained in this study improves our understanding on VOCs conversion in process furnace and its influence on in-site NOx reduction. Targeted suggestion was formulated which can promote the progresses in VOCs abatement in China.

10.21203/rs.3.rs-11191906/v1.abstract: Abstract Carbon allotropes span molecular to extended architectures, with dimensional-ity playing a central role in determining their electronic structure and chemical reactivity. Inspired by the unique electronic characteristics of carbenes and the functional diversity of carbon allotropes, we computationally design a previously unexplored zero-dimensional carbon dicarbene allotrope (CDCA) at the ωB97XD/Def2-TZVP level. CDCA is composed exclusively of carbon atoms and incorporates two electronically communicating carbene centres within a cyclic molecular framework. Density-of-states analysis and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations are employed to characterize its electronic structure, reactive sites, and structural stability. The singlet state is substantially more stable than the triplet state, while the carbon framework remains structurally stable during the investigated finite-temperature dynamics. CDCA exhibits pronounced reactivity toward SO 2 , SO 3 , NO, NO 2 , CO, CO 2 , and H 2 O through interactions involving its two carbene centres. Most notably, the two-centre architecture enables orientation-dependent activation of molecular nitrogen: interaction of N 2 with both carbene centres promotes N–N bond cleavage, whereas single-centre interaction yields an intact N 2 adduct. Subsequent stepwise hydrogenation of the activated nitrogen species provides a calculated pathway toward NH 3 formation. These results establish CDCA as a distinct zero-dimensional, carbon-only molecular architecture in which intrinsic carbene reactivity is integrated into a carbon allotrope, providing a new conceptual framework for small-molecule activation and the exploration of carbon-only systems for nitrogen chemistry.

10.26434/chemrxiv-2024-p1txk/v2.abstract: Coupling block copolymer self-assembly with ultrafast Joule heating enables second-scale crystallization of ordered mesoporous oxides while preserving long-range mesoscopic order. Using this strategy, we synthesize long-range ordered mesoporous magnesium-aluminum oxide frameworks at low magnesium contents exhibiting defect spinel-related nanocrystalline structures. Ex situ isothermal holds at 1000 to 1155 °C reveal rapid crystallite enlargement followed by a plateau in apparent crystallite size. In pure γ-alumina, this early saturation, together with retention of the ordered mesostructure, is consistent with geometrically constrained crystallite growth. Magnesium incorporation enables further crystallite enlargement before saturation, yielding larger defect-spinel-related domains while retaining long-range mesoscopic order. We further demonstrate the incorporation of in situ crystallized platinum nanoparticles within the ordered magnesium-aluminum oxide framework and their activity for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation at 350 °C. These results demonstrate that ultrafast Joule heating can access distinct crystallization trajectories in compositionally modified mesoporous oxides that are precluded by mesostructural collapse during conventional furnace heating.

10.26434/chemrxiv.15011542/v1.abstract: This study compares the alternating-magnetic-field (AMF) heating of Fe3O4-, MnFe2O4-, MgFe2O4-, and SrFe12O19-targeted nanoparticle preparations and of their sequentially silica-modified, aminated, Aufunctionalized, and PEG-treated forms. The compositions are identified by their nominal synthesis precursors. Temperature–time curves and the times required to reach 42 °C were measured in water and in nominally 1% agar phantoms under identical induction-generator settings (132 kHz; 5 kW rated output). Among the untreated preparations, the Mg-labeled series reached 42 °C fastest (145 s in water and 187 s in agar), whereas the Srlabeled series was the slowest (222 and 293 s, respectively). For the Mg-labeled particles, increasing the concentration from 2.5 to 10 mg mL 1 shortened the time to 42 °C from 394 to 77 s in water and from 381 to 112 - s in agar. In water, the aminated Mn-, Mg-, and Sr-labeled samples heated fastest within their respective surfacetreatment series (139, 124, and 209 s), whereas the unmodified Fe-labeled core was fastest within the Fe series (171 s). The PEG-treated specimens exhibited the longest times in all four water-based series. FTIR, SEM, and EDX analyses characterized the successive surface-treatment stages, including the detection of Au after functionalization. Together, these findings clarify how precursor-defined ferrite composition, concentration, surface treatment, and surrounding medium influence magnetic heating under matched apparatus conditions.

10.26434/chemrxiv.15011724/v1.abstract: Decentralized alternatives to centralized fertilizer production are needed to reduce supply chain risks, minimize transportation costs, and lower environmental impacts. Solar-powered Electrochemical Stripping (ECS) is an emerging technology that can produce ammonium fertilizer in a distributed manner through wastewater nitrogen recovery. We quantify the fraction of fertilizer demand in the United States that can be met by a wastewater feedstock while minimizing transportation distances, finding that 55% (5.54 Mt N per year) of demand is co-located with sufficient supply from domestic, agricultural, or industrial wastewater. A techno-economic assessment of ECS at scales sufficient to meet localized fertilizer demand estimated breakeven prices of US$8.70/kg N for ammonium sulfate, US$9.69/kg N for ammonium nitrate, and US$31.18/kg N for monoammonium phosphate, and US$12.15/kg N for diammonium phosphate. Integration of the techno-economic model with geospatial analysis found ECS-derived fertilizer prices ranged from 2.2x-5.5x local 2016-2026 retail prices, with ECS performing most competitively in the Pacific U.S. region. Sensitivity analysis showed improving current efficiency, increasing current density, lowering capital cost, and increasing equipment lifetime would have the greatest impact on approaching retail cost parity. This work elucidates pathways and barriers to widespread implementation of wastewater-derived fertilizers and advances United Nations Sustainable Development goals for responsible consumption and production, clean water, and zero hunger.

10.26599/nr.2026.94909308.abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic reduction of nitric oxide (NO) to ammonia (NH3) offers a sustainable, low-temperature alternative to the energy and carbon-intensive Haber-Bosch process, simultaneously facilitating green NH3 synthesis and environmental remediation under ambient conditions. This study reports the development of a metal-organic framework (MOF)-derived, hierarchically engineered hollow polyhedral CoP/Ni2P bimetallic phosphide catalyst with high activity toward the nitric oxide reduction reaction (NORR) in both neutral and acidic media. Importantly, the catalytic activity is significantly improved in acidic conditions with an NH3 yield of 68.28 μmol∙cm-2∙h-1 and Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 65.4% at −1.05 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE). The acid-enhanced performance highlights the important role of proton concentration in the NO hydrogenation steps. In addition, the CoP/Ni2P-based gas diffusion cathode in a Zn-NO battery system serves as a concentration-universal energy conversion platform that achieves high open circuit potentials of 1.56 V (neutral) and 2.00 V (acidic) with peak power densities of 2.39 mW∙cm-2 and 3.34 mW∙cm-2, respectively. Through density functional theory calculations, it is revealed that the built-in electric field-induced optimization of the d-band center at the CoP/Ni2P heterogeneous interface is determined by charge rearrangement towards Fermi level alignment. The width and shape of the d-band are correlated with the position of its center, which in turn tunes the adsorption free energies of key reaction intermediates. This study demonstrates the viability of integrating environmental pollutant remediation with sustainable ammonia production and concurrent power generation within a unified electrochemical cell and establishes MOF-derived bimetallic phosphides as a novel class of efficient NORR electrocatalysts.

10.3389/fceng.2026.1966277.abstract: The high temperature water-gas shift (HT-WGS) reaction is a central conversion step in ammonia production since it boosts the hydrogen yield and reduces the carbon monoxide content in the synthesis gas mixture before subsequent purification and ammonia synthesis. The industrial reactor was analyzed numerically with COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2. A three-dimensional model was created by combining momentum transport, heat transfer, multicomponent species transport, heterogeneous reaction kinetics, and intraparticle diffusion in porous Fe-Cr catalyst pellets under realistic adiabatic plant operating conditions. The novelty of the approach lies in combining industrial plant validation with simultaneous representation of reactor scale transport and pellet -scale diffusion-reaction processes. The model predictions were compared with the measured axial temperature profile and outlet gas composition obtained from the industrial plant. The model accurately predicted plant data with MAE = 3.50 K, R 2 = 0.950 (temperatures), and MAPE = 5.30% (outlet content). The validated model was used to examine velocity, temperature, pressure, gas-composition, gas–pellet concentration, and intraparticle concentration profiles. A parametric analysis was performed to evaluate the effects of inlet temperature and steam-to-CO ratio on CO conversion. The pressure profile demonstrated an approximately linear decrease across the catalyst bed, dropping from 30 to 28.35 bar. The mole fractions of CO and H 2 O dropped along the reactive bed, while CO 2 and H 2 rose. Increasing the inlet temperature enhanced CO conversion from about 38.5% at 618 K to around 71% at 653–658 K, while increasing the steam-to-CO ratio from 4.0 to 6.0 improved anticipated conversion from approximately 50%–70%. The validated model is a valuable tool for assessing the operation of industrial HT-WGS reactors in ammonia producing facilities.

10.3389/fpls.2026.2010688.abstract: Introduction Spatial variability in crop nitrogen (N) status limits the effectiveness of uniform fertilization in tobacco, yet remotely sensed spectral signals cannot be directly translated into crop N demand. This study developed a physiology-informed unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral framework linking leaf dry matter (LDM), leaf N concentration (LNC), the leaf nitrogen nutrition index (NNIleaf), and variable N management. Methods Field experiments involving seven N application rates (0–150 kg N ha −1 ) were conducted in Yunnan, China, during 2023–2024. A critical leaf-N relationship was established using ln(LDM) and LNC. Multispectral vegetation indices were screened using Pearson correlation analysis and recursive feature elimination. Partial least squares regression (PLSR), random forest (RF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were compared for estimating ln(LDM) and LNC, from which NNIleaf was subsequently derived. Results The four seasonal critical points obtained in 2023 were described by N c,leaf = −3.156[ln(LDM)] 2 + 32.800ln(LDM) − 25.20 (R 2 = 0.992; RMSE = 0.978 mg g −1 ). XGBoost provided the best overall performance. In the independent 2024 validation, R² values for ln(LDM), LNC, and NNIleaf were 0.826, 0.783, and 0.832, respectively, with an NRMSE of 5.51% for NNIleaf. The fitted N-response relationship identified 82.5 kg N ha −1 as the NNIleaf-defined physiological N baseline (Nphys), corresponding to the lowest total N rate at which fitted NNIleaf reached 1. In a production-scale cross-year demonstration, the NNIleaf-based strategy recommended an average of 97.12 kg N ha −1 and was associated with slightly lower N input, 3.18% higher yield, and a 2.77-percentage-point reduction in yield coefficient of variation relative to conventional management. Discussion The framework provides a physiologically interpretable link between multispectral traits, leaf N sufficiency, and spatial N recommendations. Wider validation of the critical-N relationship and same-year fertilizer comparisons remain necessary.

10.3390/molecules31213938.abstract: The development of sustainable fuels and hydrogen carriers is essential for a carbon-neutral energy future. Ammonia (NH3) is a promising energy vector, yet its synthesis remains dependent on the energy-intensive Haber–Bosch process, while nitrogen oxides (NOx) persist as major atmospheric pollutants. In this work, spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the MPWB1K/def2SVP level are used to investigate the capture and reduction of NO and NO2 within a rigid covalent organic framework (M1). Nucleus-Independent Chemical Shift (NICS) analysis reveals a strongly aromatic shielding character (NICS = −10.8) that provides a unique electronic environment, while electrostatic potential (ESP) mapping illustrates local electron density. Confinement within the framework suppresses competing pathways that preferentially favor the pathway toward NH3 and H2O. Activation barriers are significantly reduced, driven by charge transfer that weakens N–O bonds. The rigid covalent organic framework remains structurally stable throughout the process. These findings demonstrate a viable strategy for converting atmospheric pollutants into valuable energy carriers under moderate thermal activation.

10.3390/nano16221454.abstract: The electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) offers a sustainable pathway for both wastewater treatment and ammonia synthesis, yet its performance is highly sensitive to the catalyst surface structure and electrolyte composition. Here, we systematically investigate the facet-dependent activity on Cu(111), Cu(110), and Cu(100) single-crystal electrodes toward NO3RR in alkaline and bicarbonate media. Our results reveal that the activity trend for both nitrite and ammonia formation follows the order Cu(111) < Cu(110) < Cu(100) in both electrolytes. Cu(100) exhibits the highest activity for ammonia production, while Cu(111) suffers from pronounced kinetic hindrance due to the accumulation of *NOx intermediates that block the surface, leading to significant time-dependent deactivation. While (bi)carbonate anions inhibit NO3RR by competitive adsorption, they also inhibit hydrogen evolution, enabling near-100% Faradaic efficiency for nitrate conversion in KHCO3 over a broad potential window. In situ Raman spectroscopy data confirms the co-adsorption of (bi)carbonate in the potential range of NO3RR. These findings resolve existing discrepancies in the literature regarding facet-dependent NO3RR activity and provide insights for the rational design of Cu-based electrocatalysts for sustainable ammonia electrosynthesis.

10.3390/pr14213539.abstract: Joule heating coupled with porous media offers rapid in situ heat generation and a more uniform temperature distribution for DRM reactions, whereas the strong coupling of structural and operating parameters renders conventional trial-and-error optimization inefficient and costly. To tackle this challenge, a multi-physics numerical model for a centrally resistively heated DRM reactor is constructed by coupling Joule heating, flow and heat transfer, multicomponent species transport, and apparent reaction kinetics. A fully connected feedforward neural network (FC-FNN) surrogate model is further established to enable rapid prediction of reactor performance. Seven critical input variables are selected, including reaction temperature, gas hourly space velocity (GHSV), etc., and 9216 simulation samples are generated via numerical simulations for surrogate model training and parametric analysis. The results demonstrate that the Bayesian-optimized FC-FNN model exhibits high predictive accuracy for the core reactor performance metrics, achieving coefficients of determination (R2) above 0.960 for CH4 conversion, CO2 conversion, energy efficiency, and the H2/CO molar ratio. Subsequently, an unknown-constrained alternating Bayesian optimization (UCA-BO) algorithm is adopted to maximize the average reactant conversion under the constraints of H2/CO molar ratio ≥ 0.9 and bed-temperature non-uniformity ≤ 5%. Under the optimized operating conditions, the average reactant conversion reaches 94.12%, accompanied by a H2/CO molar ratio of 0.98, a bed-temperature non-uniformity of 4.53%, and a system energy efficiency of 74.83%. Posterior verification with the trained surrogate model gives slightly lower values (91.28%, 0.91, 4.86%, and 72.36%), all of which remain within the imposed constraints, confirming feasibility. Overall, the proposed integrated framework of numerical simulation, surrogate modeling, and Bayesian optimization enables efficient parameter screening and comprehensive performance optimization of resistively heated porous-media DRM systems, providing a methodological basis for the structural design and operating-parameter optimization of related reactor systems.

10.3390/systems14111407.abstract: Renewable power fluctuations and uncertain ammonia synthesis performance complicate operational coordination in green hydrogen–ammonia systems. This study develops a closed-loop prediction–scheduling framework using dual Gaussian processes to characterize renewable power and process performance. Calibrated lower and upper bounds enter material and energy constraints, while multi-objective particle swarm optimization balances operating cost and schedule variation. A joint-risk index selects plan retention, local repair, or global re-optimization, combined with plan refresh and conditional Pareto reuse in rolling horizon scheduling. The framework is evaluated with 24 h aggregated simulations using public meteorological data and published experimental data. Paired comparisons across seven fixed scenarios show that event-triggered and periodic scheduling both completed all 20 runs per scenario while satisfying all hard constraints. Under the reported serial timing protocol, event triggering reduced total controller runtime by 15.30–34.73%. Of 234 supplementary stress-test requests, 177 completed the day, including 176 that satisfied all hard constraints and one with a terminal audit failure; 57 stopped during the search. These results show that the framework coordinates probabilistic prediction, physical constraints, and scheduling responses under the specified simulation conditions, providing a reproducible approach to operational optimization of green hydrogen–ammonia systems.

10.3390/w18222814.abstract: Electrocatalytic water splitting (EWS) offers a sustainable route for green hydrogen (H2) generation; however, the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) suffers from sluggish kinetics and high thermodynamic overpotential, severely hindering overall system efficiency. Replacing the traditional OER with the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) offers a highly attractive alternative, as it lowers the cell voltage needed for hydrogen evolution and can contribute to the treatment of urea-containing wastewater, provided that urea is converted selectively to N2. This review comprehensively examines recent advances in electrocatalytic materials for urea-assisted water splitting (UAWS). It highlights key catalyst engineering strategies, including compositional tuning, heteroatom doping, and modification of structural and morphological, phase and interface properties, electronic conductivity, and durability of advanced electrocatalyst classes to accelerate UOR and hydrogen evolution. Furthermore, the work discusses degradation mechanisms, in situ characterization, interfacial dynamics, and structural effects in wastewater environments, bridging fundamental reaction mechanisms with EWS operation. By coupling hydrogen production with nitrogen removal from urea-containing wastewater, this work provides critical insights and guidelines for designing high-performance, cost-effective, and scalable resource-positive energy systems. Rather than cataloging individual studies, this review evaluates the reported catalysts against four criteria: the working anodic phase after surface reconstruction, product selectivity (N2 versus nitrite/nitrate), the test conditions behind each reported voltage saving, and the use of authentic urea-containing feeds. It also states the application scenarios in which urea oxidation is justified.

10.64509/jdi.14.173.abstract: Electrochemical hydrogen sensors are attractive for hydrogen detection owing to their high sensitivity, rapid response, and low energy consumption, offering great potential for safety monitoring in complex environments. However, the anodic HOR catalysts are highly susceptible to poisoning by interfering species such as ammonia, posing a critical challenge to the development of robust hydrogen sensors for ammonia-containing environments. Since binary transition metal elements are promising for further optimizing the HOR performance of platinum compared to single transition metals, metal salts with different combinations were dispersed on XC-72 by rotary evaporation here. After wet impregnation, FeCo-Pt, FeMn-Pt, CoMn-Pt, and Fe-Pt, were obtained by heat treatment under H2/Ar mixed gas. In this strategy, Fe and Co form an FeCo alloy during heat treatment. Compared to single-element doping, the alloyed transition metal acted as “dual-metal electron pump” further optimizes the electronic structure of Pt, thereby constructing a highly efficient composite catalyst system. This effective regulation of the electronic structure significantly enhances the electron transfer capability of Pt, ultimately achieving simultaneous improvements in the catalyst’s HOR activity and ammonia resistance, thereby enabling efficient hydrogen sensing with strong resistance to disturbance.

10.64898/2026.11.09.763769.abstract: Landfill leachate can contain high concentrations of ammonia and organic nitrogen requiring treatment before discharge. Sequencing batch reactors (SBRs) promote biological nitrogen removal through alternating aerobic and anoxic conditions, but taxonomic profiling alone cannot resolve how nitrogen transformation and competing retention pathways are distributed across microbial communities. This study applied gene-resolved metagenomics to a sludge sample collected from a UK landfill leachate SBR. Nitrogen-metabolism genes were linked to contig-level taxonomic assignments and metagenome-assembled genome bins to examine nitrification, denitrification, dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), and assimilatory nitrate reduction (ANR). Nitrogen-transformation potential was partitioned across dominant and minor taxa. Nitrospirota and Pseudomonadota were the most abundant classified phyla, whereas Actinomycetota represented only 4% of the community but included Actinomycetes, which showed the highest within-taxon proportion of nitrogen metabolism associated genes. amoABC was assigned only to Nitrosomonas and Nitrososphaerota, whereas denitrification genes were more widely distributed but frequently occurred as partial pathways. nosZ was detected only in the minor phyla Chloroflexota, Acidobacteriota and Myxococcota. DNRA and ANR-associated genes occurred across multiple lineages; nirA in Nitrospira and DNRA-associated nirBD elsewhere within Nitrospirota suggested nitrifier-associated lineages may also encode nitrogen retention potential. Gene-resolved metagenomics identified candidate low-abundance contributors, restricted distributions of genes associated with ammonia oxidation and nitrous oxide reduction, and nitrogen-retention potential not apparent from taxonomic composition alone. Because the study examined DNA-level potential in a single sludge sample, expression, reactor chemistry and longitudinal data are needed to establish pathway activity and operational relevance.
